title: Ages, Durations, and Intervals
description: Master CQL's temporal toolkit: compute ages with AgeInYearsAt, measure elapsed time with 'between', extract date components, and reason about clinical intervals with during, contains, and overlaps — the building blocks of every eCQM measurement period.
learningObjectives: Compute age at a reference date with AgeInYearsAt / AgeInMonthsAt
Measure elapsed time with 'days between' and 'difference in'
Extract components from dates with 'month from'
Filter resources by when they occurred ('during' a measurement period)
Use start of / end of on interval literals

hints.message: AgeInMonthsAt(@2024-03-12) works exactly like AgeInYearsAt but returns whole months.
days between <earlier> and <later> counts elapsed days. The birthDate needs FHIRHelpers.ToDate() to become a Date.
Extract components with: month from <date>. Other components: year, day, hour, minute.
First([Observation] O where O.effective during Interval[@2024-01-01, @2024-06-30] return O.effective as String) — 'during' is inclusive on both ends.
Last([Observation] O return O.effective as String) returns the chronologically last value.
Interval[low, high] contains <point> is true when the point falls inside (inclusive).
E.period during Interval[...] checks the WHOLE encounter period falls inside. One of the three encounters extends past June 30.
days between start of I and end of I counts ELAPSED days: 2024 is a leap year — Jan(31)+Feb(29)+Mar(31)+Apr(30)+May(31)+Jun(30) = 182 days in the period, so elapsed = 181.
A overlaps B when they share at least one point: [Jan 1, Mar 31] and [Mar 1, Jun 30] share all of March.
Interval A starts 30 days or less before start of B: Apr 1 minus Mar 1 = 31 days — so this should be false.
